correctness.rationale: A profile (i,j) is a pure Nash equilibrium precisely when j=C(i) and F(i)=R(C(i))=i. For k>=3, constant two-state F yields a single reachable equilibrium, the swap gives none, and identity F yields two distinct equilibria with a third column giving a unilateral-response trap. Thus connectivity iff F constant. The independent response map law gives Pr(constant)=(k+1)/(2k), Pr(at least one fixed point)=(3k+1)/(4k). Direct fresh directed-graph exhaustive tests for k=3,4,5,6 checked all 72,256,800,2304 response-map pairs and agree with fractions 4/5,10/13,3/4,14/19. The proof, not this finite testing, establishes all k>=3.

value.rationale: The exact conditional probability and nonzero 2/3 limit expose a genuine asymptotic regime change relative to published equal-action two-player connectivity. It is an exact natural game-graph statistic for a common asymmetric action-space model, not a renaming of the equal-action parameter.

final_claim: In the independent uniform generic ordinal 2 by k two-player game ensemble (k>=3), the conditional fraction of games with at least one pure Nash equilibrium whose strict best-response graph is connected to every equilibrium from every non-equilibrium profile is 2(k+1)/(3k+1), tending to 2/3 as k tends to infinity.
